blocks.content: The National Human Rights Commission is the watchdog of human rights in the country, embodying India's concern for the protection and promotion of human rights.

rows: Only retired Chief Justice of India
Retired Chief Justice of India OR retired Judge of Supreme Court
3 Members (at least 1 must be a woman)

items: The Protection of Human Rights (Amendment) Act, 2019 reduced the tenure of NHRC members from 5 years to 3 years.
NHRC cannot inquire into any matter after the expiry of one year from the date on which the act constituting violation of human rights is alleged to have been committed.
NHRC has limited powers and jurisdiction regarding human rights violations committed by members of the armed forces.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: NHRC is a statutory body established under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993.
The Chairperson can be a retired Chief Justice of India or a retired Judge of the Supreme Court.
The Chairperson and members hold office for a term of three years or until 70 years of age, whichever is earlier.
Appointments are made by the President on the recommendation of a six-member committee headed by the Prime Minister.
The commission's decisions and recommendations are purely advisory and recommendatory in nature.
